items.text: Uploads to the sync service keep stalling after a few failures. Can you look at the retry logic and tell me why?

tool.name: Read

items.text:
## Why the uploads stall

The retry loop in `uploadChunk` waits for the *previous* delay to finish **before** it computes the next one, so a burst of failures compounds instead of spreading out. Two things make it worse:

- the delay doubles on every attempt but is never capped
- the jitter is added to the delay instead of replacing part of it

### What I would change

1. Cap the delay at 30 seconds
2. Apply *full jitter*, a random value between zero and the capped delay
3. Stop after `maxAttempts` and surface the last error

Here is the shape of the fix:

```ts
export function nextDelay(attempt: number, base = 500, cap = 30_000): number {
  const ceiling = Math.min(cap, base * 2 ** attempt);
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * ceiling);
}
```

And how to check it from the command line:

```bash
npm test -- --grep "nextDelay"
node scripts/simulate-retries.mjs --attempts 8 --seed 7
```

| Attempt | Old delay | New ceiling |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| 1       | 500 ms    | 500 ms      |
| 4       | 4 s       | 4 s         |
| 8       | 64 s      | 30 s        |

> Backoff without a cap is a polite way of waiting forever.

The reasoning follows the [exponential backoff guide](https://example.com/docs/retries), which recommends full jitter for exactly this case.
Good catch. Fix the backoff, but keep the public API unchanged.
I'll patch the delay calculation in `backoff.ts` and run the suite.
